style: Linocut and colored-pencil narrative scenes with viewpoint diagrams
provider: Built-in image generation and deterministic SVG diagrams
note: Pictures support the lesson text and do not replace decoding or evidence from narration. Key lesson word-part examples have native editable labels; other schematic marks illustrate organization. Read sort statements in their supplied context. Educator review is pending.

sources.prompt: Square text-free children narrative illustration in expressive linocut and colored pencil style. A medium-brown-skinned girl with dark curly hair in a teal raincoat looks down at her new purple shoes splashing into a shallow sidewalk puddle. Behind her a dark-brown-skinned boy with short curly hair and a gold jacket has a small laughing smile. Scene centered on puddle and action, no portraits, no text, no speech bubbles, no numbers. Age about nine. Emotion gentle, no mocking gestures, no exaggerated caricature. Nonphotorealistic flat print texture.
sources.alt: A girl in a teal coat looks worriedly down at purple shoes splashing in a puddle; a boy in a gold jacket smiles behind her.
sources.caption: An outside view shows the shared event: Maya gets wet shoes and Dev laughs behind her. His reason and later worry come from the passage, not from reading his face. Visual viewpoint alone does not determine grammatical person.
sources.editPrompt: Edit the first of the two recent illustrations: the exterior scene with a girl stepping into a puddle and a boy behind her. Preserve composition, linocut and colored-pencil style, both characters, clothing, skin tones, setting and puddle. Change only the girl’s facial expression: mouth closed in a small downturned or neutral line, brows mildly raised toward center, looking down at her wet purple shoes with surprised embarrassment. She must NOT smile or look delighted. Preserve the boy’s mild laughing smile behind her. Keep the purple lace-up shoes. No text or additional symbols. Return only the revised exterior scene, not the downward-view image.

sources.prompt: Square text-free children narrative illustration in expressive linocut and colored pencil style. First-person visual view looking down at purple shoes worn by the viewpoint character in a shallow sidewalk puddle, teal raincoat hem visible at bottom edge. Water ripples around shoes. No face and no other people visible. Concrete subjective viewpoint, same simple warm ivory sidewalk and blue puddle palette. No text, symbols, labels, numbers or photorealism.
sources.alt: The viewer looks down past a teal coat at purple lace-up sneakers standing in a puddle.
sources.caption: Looking down at wet shoes illustrates Maya’s immediate experience. Pair it with her first-person narration in the passage. An image alone cannot establish the words I or my, or tell Dev’s thoughts.
sources.editPrompt: Edit the downward-looking first-person puddle illustration among these two recent images. Keep its framing, teal coat hem, sidewalk, puddle ripples, linocut and colored-pencil texture. Change ONLY the footwear to match the other reference scene: purple canvas high-top sneakers with white laces, white toe caps and white rubber soles, worn with dark trousers. These are soaked shoes, not waterproof rain boots. The first-person image must show the wearer looking down at both shoes. No text. Return ONLY the revised first-person downward view.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: An empty speech bubble floats above an open book.
assets.alt: An empty speech bubble floats above an open book.
assets.caption: The narrator is the storytelling voice. A bubble is a reminder of voice, not proof that a character is speaking aloud.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: Two different window frames overlap different edges of one blue puddle.
assets.alt: Two different window frames overlap different edges of one blue puddle.
assets.caption: Different perspectives can emphasize different information. Visual viewpoint is an analogy; grammatical person is established by the narrator’s wording.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: A schematic page has a single highlighted line among surrounding lines.
assets.alt: A schematic page has a single highlighted line among surrounding lines.
assets.caption: Inspect pronouns referring to the narrator outside dialogue. I inside a quotation, or she describing another person, does not by itself identify the narration.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: Two simple figures have different clothing colors and skin tones.
assets.alt: Two simple figures have different clothing colors and skin tones.
assets.caption: Characters take part in the story. These schematic figures are reminders, not portraits or evidence of their personalities.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: Two empty speech bubbles face toward the middle at different heights.
assets.alt: Two empty speech bubbles face toward the middle at different heights.
assets.caption: Dialogue records characters’ speech. Read the quoted words and the narrator’s words separately when identifying point of view.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: An empty cloud-shaped thought bubble has two smaller circles below it.
assets.alt: An empty cloud-shaped thought bubble has two smaller circles below it.
assets.caption: Thoughts are not directly visible in a face. A text may report them; first-person narration may infer them or recount what someone later explained.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: A rectangular frame contains a blue puddle.
assets.alt: A rectangular frame contains a blue puddle.
assets.caption: A scene focuses on connected action at a particular place and time. The illustration is a cue to the supplied puddle scene.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: Three boxes connect in a left-to-right sequence.
assets.alt: Three boxes connect in a left-to-right sequence.
assets.caption: Keep the supplied events consistent while changing the narrator. Identify new information as a plausible invention if the source does not state it.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: Two teal frames each contain a gold circle in the same position.
assets.alt: Two teal frames each contain a gold circle in the same position.
assets.caption: Compare the two narrations for shared events and different information. This diagram highlights a shared feature, not identical stories.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: Matching teal frames contain different inner shapes.
assets.alt: Matching teal frames contain different inner shapes.
assets.caption: Contrast what each telling includes and how it feels. Difference does not automatically mean dishonesty, or prove both accounts correct.

assets.alt: A gold bus has three blue windows and two visible wheels.
assets.caption: The pronoun We in the narration identifies the first-person group. A bus picture alone cannot establish narrator or an exact ten-second delay.

assets.alt: An empty speech bubble sits apart from a figure facing forward.
assets.caption: The card says she pretended not to hear. That intention is supplied by the text, not observable from the picture alone.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: One schematic raised hand has curved motion lines on either side.
assets.alt: One schematic raised hand has curved motion lines on either side.
assets.caption: The card describes shaking hands and uses My. Shaking does not always mean fear; identify the narrator from the wording.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: A cake has a missing bite-shaped section on one side.
assets.alt: A cake has a missing bite-shaped section on one side.
assets.caption: The narrator reports something the characters do not know: the dog ate the cake. Do not infer a narrator’s knowledge from cake artwork alone.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: An empty speech bubble sits above a separate smaller thought cloud.
assets.alt: An empty speech bubble sits above a separate smaller thought cloud.
assets.caption: A character’s spoken words can differ from their feelings. Read I told to identify first person; use the text to establish the disagreement.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: A simple smiling face sits beside an empty thought cloud.
assets.alt: A simple smiling face sits beside an empty thought cloud.
assets.caption: The card explicitly says Priya smiles while feeling angry. A smile alone cannot establish feelings; naming Priya in this narration signals third person.

assets.alt: A plain gold object sits between two right-pointing arrows.
assets.caption: A transfer cue for Hand it over. The words I said outside the quotation identify first-person narration.
